correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.finding: @empressaio/setback-corpus's max_lot_coverage_pct field carries a documented NOT_SPECIFIED sentinel semantic (table-types.d.ts: 'Set true when the value is the NOT_SPECIFIED sentinel (honest gap)'), flagged via provenance.max_lot_coverage_pct.not_specified. Live count across the whole corpus: 199 of 274 districts (73%) carry this flag, including districts whose value is nonzero and whose own quote text describes a real cited figure (e.g. every Austin district) alongside districts where the value is a literal 0 placeholder for a field the ordinance never models at all (Bastrop's 4 districts: 'a separate lot-coverage percentage is not modeled as a distinct scalar here', real value lives under max_impervious_pct, a DIFFERENT regulatory metric this job's maxLotCoveragePct rail must not silently substitute).
correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.consequence: This job treats not_specified as authoritative over the numeric value for maxLotCoveragePct specifically (and, by the same field-level contract, maxFootprintSqFt wherever it depends on that field) -- writing absent-verified rather than value whenever the flag is set, regardless of whether the accompanying number looks plausible. Not auditing/fixing the corpus's own internal consistency (why a real-looking Austin value still carries the flag) -- reading its own documented contract as written, the same discipline S1 applied to the corpus's setback fields (which do not exhibit this issue in the samples checked).
correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.populationImpact: Likely a real, sizeable class of absent-verified maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt cells even in ruled-table cities where every setback scalar resolves cleanly -- will be counted and reported exactly, not smoothed over.

correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.finding: The dispatch's STANDING FACTS never name a dependency for buildableAreaSqFt/buildableAreaPct beyond 'you write cells' -- but the ONLY validated, tested buildable-envelope area computation in this program (the envelope-saga's per-edge half-plane-clipping offset, 12/12 unanimous close, 2026-08-07) requires per-edge FRONT/SIDE/REAR/CORNER labeling, which in turn requires road-frontage data (OSM Overpass fetch, legacy-design-tools buildableEnvelope/roads.ts + roadClassify.ts + roadClassSetbacks.ts) that this job does not integrate and was never scoped to acquire. nodeFacetBakeTier1.ts's own comment names the retired method it replaced as a 'labeling x district product' -- i.e. a real edge-aware computation existed and was deliberately cut (anti-zombie, Master WDLL 3.7/I-A) in favor of the atom chain, which is itself held.
correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.consequence: A uniform (non-edge-aware) buffer using any single setback distance was considered and rejected: using the smallest setback overstates buildable area (optimistic, unsafe direction); using the largest collapses many real, buildable lots to a false zero (a different serious inaccuracy). Full road-aware edge labeling is out of reach without either lifting the held atom writer (explicitly prohibited) or building a new, independently-fetched OSM/road-classification pipeline this dispatch never budgeted (effectively rebuilding the atom writer's own machinery in a second location).
correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.proposedDesign: Port (faithfully, cited by file/line, matching S1's own precedent for setback-table-router.mjs) the SAME reference module's lowest-confidence, dependency-free tier: buildableEnvelope/geometry.ts's insetPerEdge (pure, DB-free, its only external dependency is the public npm package polygon-clipping, already used by legacy-design-tools) plus buildableEnvelope/edgeLabeling.ts's shape-only front/rear inference (frontFromShape + labelFromFront -- pure geometry, no OSM/road fetch, no private package import). Applied uniformly (this job never integrates road or geocoded-point signals, so every parcel resolves via the shape tier, honestly, not selectively). Every buildableAreaSqFt/buildableAreaPct value cell's envelopeDisclosure names the method explicitly ('shape-only edge inference, confidence ~0.35, no road-frontage data integrated; full precision requires the atom chain's road-aware pipeline, held') so nothing is served as more certain than it is -- this is a real, cited, already-tested algorithm's own documented low tier, not an invented shortcut.
correctionsAndFindingsNotInTheDispatch.scopeNote: parcelAreaSqFt, maxHeightFt, and maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt do NOT depend on this -- parcelAreaSqFt is pure geometry (real value for every in-city parcel with usable txgio_parcel geometry, ruled-table city or not); maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct are direct corpus district lookups reusing S1's own resolveSetbackForParcel/getSetbackTableForZoning (no second resolver). proposedRailDesign.parcelAreaSqFt: Real geometry fact, independent of zoning/ruled-table status. Fetch every txgio_parcel geometry fragment for the prop_id (no PostGIS ST_Area call -- raw GeoJSON ring fetched to JS, area computed via the ported ringAreaSqFt shoelace, matching the Geometry Law's 'truth is the raw ring' / scale-correct-numerics rule), summed across fragments. value when >0 finite; absent-verified (basis: no usable txgio_parcel geometry for this prop_id) otherwise. Written for EVERY in-city parcel in scope, ruled-table city or not.
proposedRailDesign.maxHeightFt: Direct corpus district lookup via S1's own resolveSetbackForParcel/getSetbackTableForZoning (imported, not reimplemented), reading d.max_height_ft. value when a district resolves; absent-verified when the city has no ruled table or the district code does not resolve to a row (mirrors S1's own absent-verified reasons exactly); deferred when zoningDistrict is not yet resolved (same S1 dependency).
proposedRailDesign.maxLotCoveragePct: Same lookup, d.max_lot_coverage_pct, GATED on provenance.max_lot_coverage_pct.not_specified per the finding above -- absent-verified (basis: corpus sentinel, cites the not_specified flag) when set, value otherwise.
proposedRailDesign.maxFootprintSqFt: Derived: parcelAreaSqFt x maxLotCoveragePct / 100. value only when BOTH inputs are value; otherwise inherits the blocking input's disposition (absent-verified if maxLotCoveragePct is absent-verified; deferred if either input is deferred).
proposedRailDesign.buildableAreaSqFt / buildableAreaPct: Shape-only ported inset (see finding above), consuming S1's four already-written setback scalar cells (front/side/rear/corner) as insetFeetForLabeling's input. value (with envelopeDisclosure naming the shape-only method) when the inset is non-degenerate; a distinct 'no-buildable-area' value-with-zero-area disposition (not absent-verified -- a real computation ran and found the setbacks consume the lot, matching geometry.ts's own emptyReason vocabulary) when insetPerEdge reports empty; absent-verified when the underlying setback cells themselves are absent-verified (no ruled table); deferred when setbacks are deferred (zoningDistrict blocked).
proposedRailDesign.envelopeStatus / envelopeDisclosure: Companion narrative pair summarizing which of the above happened and why, always written alongside buildableAreaSqFt (same disposition), never independently unaccounted once buildableAreaSqFt has a determination.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: A corpus field's own documented sentinel flag (not_specified) can be set on entries whose accompanying number looks real and whose quote text describes a real citation -- the flag's own type-level contract, not the number's plausibility, is the thing to trust. 199 of 274 corpus districts carry this flag on max_lot_coverage_pct.

When a mission cites a vacuous function as 'do not make it work,' read what it REPLACED (git blame / the module's own doc comment), not just what it currently returns -- nodeFacetBakeTier1.ts's comment named the retired 'labeling x district product' method, which led straight to the real, already-tested, still-portable geometry.ts/edgeLabeling.ts pair one directory over.

A pure, DB-free, dependency-free (or public-npm-only) geometry/math module in a sibling repo is safe to port-and-cite even when the business logic built on top of it (district routing, road fetching) is not -- the S1 precedent (setback-table-router.mjs) generalizes past routing logic to geometry primitives.
